title: Logic Gates & Boolean Algebra
tagline: How AND, OR, and NOT gates — made from transistors — perform every computation a CPU ever runs.

sections.content:
Every addition, comparison, and branch inside a CPU boils down to a handful of simple **logic gates**. A gate takes one or two binary inputs and produces one binary output according to a fixed rule. Chain millions of them together and you get arithmetic, memory, and control flow.

**Boolean algebra** is the mathematical language of gates — it lets you reason about binary logic with symbols, simplify complex expressions, and prove two circuits are equivalent.

sections.title: Light Switches Wired Together
sections.content: AND is two switches in series: light on only when both are closed. OR is two switches in parallel: light on when either is closed. NOT simply inverts — switch open means light on. No new physics; just different wiring. Gates work the same way, just at nanosecond speed and nanometre scale.

The five gates to know: **AND** (1 only when all inputs are 1), **OR** (1 when any input is 1), **NOT** (inverts one input), **XOR** (1 when inputs differ), **NAND** (NOT of AND — the universal gate that can build any other).

**Boolean algebra** maps directly: AND = A·B, OR = A+B, NOT = ¬A. Key laws for simplification: De Morgan's (¬(A·B) = ¬A+¬B), double negation (¬¬A = A). Fewer gates = less area, power, and delay.

Real impact: XOR checks parity (error detection). NAND builds flip-flops (memory bits). A half-adder is XOR (sum) + AND (carry). Chain full-adders and you add any 64-bit integer.

sections.explanation: JS's &, |, ^ apply logic gates in parallel to every bit of an integer. halfAdder shows how XOR+AND compose into 1-bit arithmetic — the primitive the CPU's full adder is built from.

sections.label: Concept

sections.content: Interview insight: NAND is 'universal' — any computation can be built from NAND gates alone. Early CMOS chips used only NAND to simplify fabrication. Memorise De Morgan's laws — they appear in both circuit design and boolean query optimisation (SQL WHERE clause simplification).

items: AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND are the five fundamental gates — each maps binary inputs to one binary output.
Boolean algebra (·, +, ¬) lets you simplify circuits mathematically without building them.
De Morgan's: ¬(A·B) = ¬A+¬B and ¬(A+B) = ¬A·¬B — distribute NOT and flip the operator.
Half-adder = XOR (sum) + AND (carry); full-adders chain to add multi-bit integers in the ALU.
NAND is universal — any logic function can be constructed from NAND gates alone.

quiz.question: What does an AND gate output when A=1, B=0?
quiz.explanation: AND outputs 1 only when ALL inputs are 1. With B=0, the output is 0.

quiz.question: Which gate outputs 1 when its two inputs are DIFFERENT?
quiz.explanation: XOR (exclusive OR) outputs 1 only when inputs differ: (0,1)→1, (1,0)→1, (0,0)→0, (1,1)→0.

quiz.question: Which gate combination forms a half-adder?
quiz.explanation: XOR produces the sum bit, AND produces the carry bit — together they perform 1-bit binary addition.

quiz.question: Which De Morgan's law is correct?
options: NOT(A AND B) = NOT(A) AND NOT(B)
NOT(A OR B) = NOT(A) OR NOT(B)
NOT(A AND B) = NOT(A) OR NOT(B)
NOT(A AND B) = A OR B
quiz.explanation: De Morgan: ¬(A·B) = ¬A + ¬B. Negation distributes and flips AND ↔ OR.

quiz.question: Why is NAND called a 'universal gate'?
options: Any logic function can be built from NAND gates alone
quiz.explanation: NAND is functionally complete — AND, OR, NOT, and any combination can be constructed using only NAND gates.

quiz.question: What does a NOT gate do?
quiz.explanation: NOT (inverter) has one input and flips it: 0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 0.

quiz.question: In JavaScript, which operator performs bitwise AND?
quiz.explanation: & is bitwise AND applied to every bit pair. && is logical AND (boolean short-circuit, not bitwise).

quiz.question: What is 0b1010 XOR 0b1100 in decimal?
quiz.explanation: 1010 XOR 1100 = 0110 = 6. XOR sets bits where corresponding inputs differ.

quiz.question: An OR gate with A=0, B=0 outputs:
quiz.explanation: OR outputs 1 when ANY input is 1. With both inputs 0, the output is 0.

quiz.question: XOR gates are used in which real-world application?
quiz.explanation: XOR across data bits produces a parity bit. Re-computing on read detects single-bit errors — used in RAM, networking, and storage.
